newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CYCLING-BOLAND TOUR MAKES BELATED START.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-BOLAND TOUR MAKES BELATED START.

text.p: Pre-race favourite Nicola Minali of Italy won the 121.9 km first stage as the Boland Bank International Cycle Tour made a belated competitive start in Paarl on Monday.
Sunday's criterium around an 800m course at Cape Town's V and A Waterfront had been treated as an exhibition by tour cyclists after the course had been declared too dangerous to race seriously.

The tight, cobblestoned stage was taken out of the general classification minutes before the scheduled start. During the subsequent exhibition race on the course one competitor wore a plastic traffic cone on his head while Minali sang to spectators.
Highest placed South African after Monday's serious racing was Gary Beneke who finished in 16th, one minute 34 seconds behind Minali.
First stage (121.9km Paarl to Riebeek Kasteel):

1 Nicola Minali (Italy) 2hrs 53mins 28secs; 2 Steven De Jongh (Netherlands) same time; 3 Frank Schinck (Germany) same time; 4 Edwin Ophof (Netherlands) same time; 5 Magnus Backstedt (Sweden) same time; 6 Mauro Bettin (Italy) + 22secs; 7 Frank Hoj (Denark) + 22secs; 8 Rob Hayles (Britain) + 22 secs; 9 Steffen Kjaergaard (Norway) + 38secs; 10 Mark Walsham (Britain) + 57secs.
